title: The oiler Kazahaya, 6 October 1943
eyebrow: North-west of Truk · two boats, each alone

participants.name: Kazahaya
participants.note: the Navy's fleet oiler, on passage to Truk, sailing alone (jacar:C08030101300); the silhouette is the kit's generic tanker, not her own outline

paras.text: The fleet oiler Kazahaya, sailing alone for Truk, met two American submarines on 6 October 1943, each on its own patrol. STEELHEAD hit her first, before dawn; TINOSA found her that morning and attacked twice, and she sank in the evening. The boats' war patrol reports beside her own signals, kept in the 2nd Destroyer Squadron's diary, on one GMT clock.

Kazahaya's signals: torpedoed in the early morning, hit again at 1105 (TINOSA's morning attack, three hits), the boiler room torpedoed at 1727, and sunk at 1830 (Tokyo time); five hits in four engagements by her own count; the captain and 122 rescued, and later counts of 154 and 98 by the two destroyers sent to her (jacar:C08030101300). JANAC credits the sinking to TINOSA and STEELHEAD jointly.

Positions are each boat's own dead reckoning and Kazahaya's signalled positions. STEELHEAD's report types her attack at 10-26N 146-29.5E; Kazahaya's first signal puts her torpedoing at 10-30N 146-37E, about 8 nm off.

STEELHEAD kept zone K (−10) and TINOSA zone K in her narrative (her tables GCT); the Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9). STEELHEAD fired at 0236 K, 0136 I: the Navy's summary has the first attack at 0140 I and Kazahaya's own summary of her loss counts "from 0100", but the destroyer squadron's log has her torpedoed at 0244 I, 68 minutes later, perhaps the time of the signal rather than the hit. Kazahaya's times for TINOSA's attacks match TINOSA's narrative an hour apart, the difference between the zones.

War patrol reports, NARA microfilm M1752 (STEELHEAD 74851315, TINOSA 74856215). The 2nd Destroyer Squadron's war diary and the Navy's October 1943 summary via JACAR (National Institute for Defense Studies). FRUPAC war map, October 3-6, 1943 (Portal to Texas History), linked from TINOSA's records. JANAC (1947), a postwar list.

events.title: Attack 1
events.words: Torpedo attack No. 1, TIME 02-36-30(K): four stern torpedoes at a single unescorted tanker, range 1100 yards; two hits and a dud; claims one damaged, 'later reported sunk by U.S.S. TINOSA'. Narrative (p04): 0236 fired four from stern tubes, 0237 saw and heard two hits, a third struck the forecastle and did not explode, 0238 target opened fire with bow gun, 0238-30 dove to 80 feet

outcome.note: Fired four stern torpedoes at 02-36-30 K (0136 I) at 10-26N 146-29.5E, a single unescorted tanker, two hits and a dud; the order has Kazahaya torpedoed once at 0244 I at 10-30N 146-37E, about 8 nm away. Hit, not probable: no other boat is known to have attacked her before TINOSA's 1101 I, and STEELHEAD's narrative heard the target "running irregularly" after the hits, as the order has her able to proceed. The times are 68 minutes apart (japanese.yml header); the place, the lone tanker and the day carry the pairing
The Navy's summary starts the attacks at 0140 I, four minutes after STEELHEAD fired (0136 I). It repeats the Combined Fleet's signals (J03), so it is the same witness, not a second one

She sank at 1830 I, after TINOSA's three attacks (ss-283-tinosa/patrol-3:Attack 2, Attack 3A-3F). STEELHEAD's hit began it ("from 0100 yesterday", the first of four engagements) and slowed her, but the loss can't be given to one attack. JANAC credits her jointly to TINOSA and STEELHEAD (janac:6/p56); ComSubPac credited STEELHEAD with a tanker damaged, 10,500 tons (endorsement, rg367-74851315/p37)

events.title: Kazahaya
events.words: The special service ship Kazahaya (12,000 tons, 16.5 knots, TO), on passage alone to Truk, was attacked by an enemy submarine 250 miles north-west of Truk (GF). She ran over one of the enemy and attacked it effectively, but took five torpedoes in all and sank at 1830
events.original: 特務艦風早（一二〇〇〇屯 一六．五節 TO）ハ単独トラックニ向ケ航行中トラックノNW二五〇′ニテ敵潜ノ襲撃ヲウク（GF） 敵一隻ヲ乗切リ有効ナル攻撃ヲ加ヘシモ前後五本ノ魚雷ヲ蒙リ一八三〇沈没
events.translation: The special service ship Kazahaya (12,000 tons, 16.5 knots, TO), on passage alone to Truk, was attacked by an enemy submarine 250 miles north-west of Truk (GF). She ran over one of the enemy and attacked it effectively, but took five torpedoes in all and sank at 1830
events.note: TINOSA's J08 (handwritten; numerals as written in Arabic figures on the page). `time` is the entry's, 0140, the start of the attacks: four minutes after STEELHEAD fired at 0136 I (0236 K). "On passage alone" fits the sheet's "Single tanker, unescorted". Compiled from the Combined Fleet's signals, so it counts once with J03. The 250 miles north-west of Truk is the day's later attacks (TINOSA's, near 10-20N 148-30E), not STEELHEAD's position, which is about 360 nm from Truk

events.translation: The special service ship Kazahaya (12,000 tons, 16.5 knots, TO), on passage alone to Truk, was attacked by an enemy submarine 250 miles north-west of Truk (GF). She ran over one of the enemy and attacked it effectively, but took five torpedoes in all and sank at 1830
events.note: The Navy's day-by-day summary of escort and anti-submarine events, October 1943 (handwritten; numerals here as written, in Arabic figures on the page: 12000, 16.5, 250, 1830). `time` is the entry's, 0140: the start of the attacks, as her own "from 0100 yesterday" (J06). Compiled from the Combined Fleet's signals ("(GF)"), so it repeats J06 and counts once with it, not as a second witness. 250 miles north-west of Truk is about 10-20N 148-50E, within about 25 miles of where TINOSA's table puts her attacks of that day (10-35N 148-30E, 10-01N 148-31E)

events.title: Kazahaya
events.words: YB signal order No. 36: the commander of the 2nd Destroyer Squadron is to send one destroyer at once to escort Kazahaya (torpedoed once at 0244 at 10°30'N 146°37'E; able to proceed under her own power)
events.original: YB信令第三六號 二水戦司令官ハ速ニ駆逐艦一隻ヲ派遣風早（〇二四四一〇度三〇分北一四六度三七分東ニ於テ雷撃一ヲ受ク自力航行可能）ノ護衛ニ任ゼシムベシ
events.translation: YB signal order No. 36: the commander of the 2nd Destroyer Squadron is to send one destroyer at once to escort Kazahaya (torpedoed once at 0244 at 10°30'N 146°37'E; able to proceed under her own power)
events.note: TINOSA's J01, the order of 6 October 0830. The position is about 8 nm east-north-east of the 10-26N 146-29.5E STEELHEAD's attack sheet types (rg367-74851315/p22). One torpedo hit, where the sheet has two hits and a dud (Hit, Hit, Dud, Miss) and the narrative a third torpedo striking the forecastle without exploding (p04); "able to proceed under her own power" fits the narrative: 0238 K "Target opened fire with bow gun and turned towards us", and the heavier screws "running irregularly" heard after 0246 K (p05). The time is 68 minutes after STEELHEAD's 0136 I (0236 K): see the header

events.title: Kazahaya
events.words: YB signal order No. 36: the commander of the 2nd Destroyer Squadron is to send one destroyer at once to escort Kazahaya (torpedoed once at 0244 at 10°30'N 146°37'E; able to proceed under her own power)

events.translation: YB signal order No. 36: the commander of the 2nd Destroyer Squadron is to send one destroyer at once to escort Kazahaya (torpedoed once at 0244 at 10°30'N 146°37'E; able to proceed under her own power)
events.note: The order of 6 October 0830 (sender YB, as written). The attack is STEELHEAD's, which is not in these records. The log has one torpedo; TINOSA's report has STEELHEAD hit her three times (remarks, rg367-74856215/p16; first endorsement, p34). The 1st Fleet's order of 0845 repeats the position (p23). The squadron sent DesDiv 24's Suzukaze (二四駆（涼風）ハ速ニ出撃, 0910, p22), which signalled 我出撃ス, "we sortie", at 1035 (p23). TINOSA sighted the tanker at 0524 K (0424 I) and typed her at 10-24N 146-52E, about 15 nm east of this position (ship contact 3, rg367-74856215/p13)

events.title: Ship contact (3)
events.words: Tanker, 10000 (plus) tons; course 85, speed 16K; loaded. The narrative (p05) picks her up by sight at 0524 K

events.title: Attack 2
events.words: Summary of attacks: 6 Torpex Mk XVIII fired, 4 hits; AO, damaged 10000 plus; range 1540. The narrative (p06) fires six bow tubes at 1201 K

outcome.note: TINOSA fired six at 1201 K (table 0204 GCT) and heard three explosions and a dud (narrative, rg367-74856215/p06); Kazahaya signalled three hits at 1210 I (J02) and put the attack at 1105 I (J04, J06), TINOSA's 1201-1204 K less the hour between the zones. Her 1200 position, 10-30N 148-20E, is about 11 nm from the table's 10-35N 148-30E. She claimed the submarine sunk by depth charges (J04); TINOSA took four close charges at 1209 K

events.title: Ship attacked
events.words: 6 (a red star on the point marked 6 of the route labelled 271500; the next point 1900 / 6)
events.note: The note gives no time; drawn at the time of the attack it is tied to (Attack 2). The position is read off the map from where the mark sits (about ±0.1–0.3°), not the note's. A route plotted from a message, its points numbered by day, ending at Truk after 1900 on the 6th; the red star marks the day-6 point. Its date-time group, 271500, fits the intercept combinedfleet describes for Kazahaya (a message decrypted on 27 September giving her departure from Kure on the 30th at 14.5 knots, due at Truk at 0700 on the 7th): candidate, because the ship's name was not in the view read. The star is the route's planned point, not a reported one: Kazahaya was torpedoed on the 6th at 0244 I at 10-30N 146-37E (STEELHEAD; japanese.yml J01), at 1105 I near 10-30N 148-20E (TINOSA's Attack 2; J02) and sank at 1830 I near 9-50N 148-24E (J05, J06), all within about 100 nm of it
events.pos_note: The position is read off the map from where the mark sits (about ±0.1–0.3°), not the note's.

events.title: Kazahaya
events.words: Flooded up to the upper-deck line, list ten degrees. Our speed seven knots. An enemy submarine is dogging us. Request escort by aircraft and destroyers urgently
events.original: 上甲板線迄浸入傾斜十度 我速力七節敵潜水艦ツキマトフ至急飛行機駆逐艦ノ護衛ヲ乞フ
events.translation: Flooded up to the upper-deck line, list ten degrees. Our speed seven knots. An enemy submarine is dogging us. Request escort by aircraft and destroyers urgently
events.note: Telegram of 1200 (the number is cut off at the top of the page). TINOSA at 1215 K: "Target had slowed, tracking about nine knots, and was headed southwest" (rg367-74856215/p06); her remarks: "slowed her to nine knots and finally to six" (p30)

events.title: Kazahaya
events.words: Kazahaya secret telegram 061210: we have been torpedoed by an enemy submarine, three hits, our ability to steam is in doubt. 10°30'N 148°20'E
events.original: 風早機密第〇六一二一〇番電 我敵潜ノ雷撃ヲ受ク三発命中航行覚束ナシ 北緯一〇度三〇分東経一四八度二〇分
events.translation: Kazahaya secret telegram 061210: we have been torpedoed by an enemy submarine, three hits, our ability to steam is in doubt. 10°30'N 148°20'E
events.note: 1210 is the telegram's time; her later telegrams put this attack at 1105 (J04, J06), which is TINOSA's Attack 2 (narrative 1201 K, 1101 I; table 0204 GCT, 1104 I). The Combined Fleet's order of 1352 (p25) gives 10°30'N 148°20'E as her 1200 position. TINOSA's table types 10-35N 148-30E. Three hits, as TINOSA heard three explosions and a dud (narrative, rg367-74856215/p06)

events.title: Kazahaya
events.words: Kazahaya secret telegram 061400: the enemy submarine that torpedoed us at 1105 certainly sunk by depth-charge attack. The sea is washing the upper deck, pumping is impossible, the ship is gradually settling. 10°16'N 148°14'E
events.original: 風早機密第〇六一四〇〇番電 一一〇五雷撃ノ敵潜水艦一隻爆雷攻撃ニ依リ確実ニ撃沈 海水上甲板ヲ洗ヒポンプ排水不可能除々ニ艦?沈下ス 北緯一〇度一六分東経一四八度一四分
events.translation: Kazahaya secret telegram 061400: the enemy submarine that torpedoed us at 1105 certainly sunk by depth-charge attack. The sea is washing the upper deck, pumping is impossible, the ship is gradually settling. 10°16'N 148°14'E
events.note: The second figure of 1105 is faint; her telegram of 0230 on the 7th (J06) gives 1105 for the same attack. TINOSA was not sunk: at 1209 K she took four depth charges, "all close", and a fire in the motor room (rg367-74856215/p06). One character before 沈下ス is not read. Her telegram of 1410 (p24) gives her 2100 position as 9°50'N 148°50'E, course 090, seven knots. From 1200 (J02) to this 1400 position she made about 14 nm to the south-south-west

events.title: Ship contact ((later))
events.words: Same tanker (contact 3, second line)

events.title: Attack 3A
events.words: Summary of attacks: 4 Torpex Mk XIV fired, 2 hits; range 1630 (narrative p07: four stern tubes at 1818 K, two hits)

outcome.note: DesDiv 24 gives 1727 I as the time of her engagement with the submarine (J05). 3A fired four at 1818 K (1718 I), two seen to hit (remarks, rg367-74856215/p17); 3B fired two at 1825 K (1725 I), none seen. The record doesn't say which, so both are possible

Kazahaya sank at 1830 I (J06), TINOSA's 1933 K "Target disappeared, sinking by the stern" (p08). JANAC credits her jointly to TINOSA and STEELHEAD (janac:6/p56: 6 October 1943, Kazahaya, tanker, 8,000 tons, 10-01N 148-31E, "Tinosa Steelhead", sunk), and in the merchant list to "Submarine", not marked probable, at 8,000e tons (janac:4/p45). Probable, not hit: STEELHEAD hit her first (J01), so the loss can't be given to one attack. Her own count is five hits in four engagements (J06): if that is one of STEELHEAD's and three of TINOSA's morning attack, one hit was made in the evening, against the four TINOSA's table claims for 3A, 3D and 3F. The second endorsement credits TINOSA with "1 AO (Type undetermined) 10,000 tons" sunk (p35); her crew called her "the OBSTINATE MARU" (p30)

events.title: Attack 3B
events.words: Summary of attacks: 2 Torpex Mk XVIII fired, 0 hits; range 1350 (narrative p07: two bow tubes at 1825 K)

outcome.note: Fired at 1825 K (1725 I) at 1,350 yards, about a minute's run before the 1727 I of J05, which Kazahaya's own summary calls the boiler room torpedoed (J06). The table claims 0 hits; the commanding officer believed "these mark XVIII may have hit because shortly thereafter the ship stopped dead in the water" (remarks, rg367-74856215/p17). The time fits 3B better than 3A, but a minute or two in a telegram's time can't settle it, so both stay possible

events.title: Kazahaya
events.words: DesDiv 24 secret telegram 062010: at 2145 arrived at Kazahaya's estimated position of distress (1727, the point of engagement with the enemy submarine, 9°50'N 148°24'E) but she is not in sight; now searching. Request aircraft cooperation from tomorrow morning
events.original: 二四駆機密第〇六二〇一〇番電 二一四五風早遭難推定位置（一七二七敵潜水艦ト交戦地點九度五〇分N一四八度二四分E）ニ到着セシモ見当ラズ今ヨリ捜索ス 明朝ヨリ飛行機ノ協力ヲ得度
events.translation: DesDiv 24 secret telegram 062010: at 2145 arrived at Kazahaya's estimated position of distress (1727, the point of engagement with the enemy submarine, 9°50'N 148°24'E) but she is not in sight; now searching. Request aircraft cooperation from tomorrow morning
events.note: `time` is the engagement's, 1727. The telegram is numbered 062010 but its text reads 2145 for the arrival, so one of the two is misread or mistyped; neither is used. TINOSA fired 3(a) at 1818 K (1718 I) and 3(b) at 1825 K (1725 I) (rg367-74856215/p07). The position is about 13 nm south-west of the 10-01N 148-31E that TINOSA's table types for every evening attack

events.title: Attack 3C
events.words: Summary of attacks: 1 Torpex Mk XIV fired, 0 hits; range 800 (narrative p07: one stern tube at 1834 K)

events.title: Attack 3D
events.words: Summary of attacks: 1 Torpex Mk XIV fired, 1 hit; range 1680 (narrative p07: stern tube at 1859 K)

outcome.note: One hit by the table, heard by sound and the control room, not seen at the periscope (rg367-74856215/p07). At 1859 K, 1759 I, half an hour before she sank. Probable for the same reason as 3A

events.title: Attack 3E
events.words: Summary of attacks: 1 Torpex Mk XVIII fired, 0 hits; range 1200 (narrative p07: bow tube at 1910 K)

events.title: Attack 3F
events.words: Summary of attacks: 1 Torpex Mk XVIII fired, 1 hit; sunk 10000 plus, same as 2; range 800 (narrative p08: second bow tube at 1913 K; target disappeared, sinking by the stern, at 1933 K)

outcome.note: The table puts the sinking against this shot ("10000 plus same as 2"), but nothing was heard or seen of it (narrative, rg367-74856215/p08); the remarks give the sinking to "one of these last two torpedoes" (3E or 3F, p18). At 1913 K, 1813 I, seventeen minutes before the 1830 I of J06. Probable for the same reason as 3A

events.title: Kazahaya
events.words: 1. From 0100 yesterday sighted six enemy submarines and engaged them four times; torpedo hits five in all. 2. 1727 boiler room torpedoed, 1830 sank. 3. Disposal of secret documents completed. 4. At 1105, in the third engagement, ran over one enemy submarine; depth-charge attack effective, certain
events.original: 二四駆機密第〇七〇二三〇番電 一、昨〇一〇〇以後敵潜水艦六隻ヲ見四回ニ亘リテ交戦被雷計五 二、一七二七罐室被雷一八三〇沈没 三、機密図書処分完了 四、一一〇五第三回交戦ノ際敵潜水艦一隻ヲ乗切リ爆雷攻撃効果確実
events.translation: 1. From 0100 yesterday sighted six enemy submarines and engaged them four times; torpedo hits five in all. 2. 1727 boiler room torpedoed, 1830 sank. 3. Disposal of secret documents completed. 4. At 1105, in the third engagement, ran over one enemy submarine; depth-charge attack effective, certain
events.note: TINOSA's J06, telegram of 7 October 0230, sender 風早 (Kazahaya). "From 0100 yesterday" opens her day with STEELHEAD's attack (0136 I). The 1105 engagement she calls the third is TINOSA's Attack 2, so the first and second were before it; only STEELHEAD's is known. Of the five hits, J01 gives STEELHEAD one and TINOSA's morning attack three (TINOSA's J02). She sank at 1830 I, sixteen hours after STEELHEAD's attack and about 120 nm east of it

events.words: 1. From 0100 yesterday sighted six enemy submarines and engaged them four times; torpedo hits five in all. 2. 1727 boiler room torpedoed, 1830 sank. 3. events.translation: 1. From 0100 yesterday sighted six enemy submarines and engaged them four times; torpedo hits five in all. 2. 1727 boiler room torpedoed, 1830 sank. 3. Disposal of secret documents completed. 4. At 1105, in the third engagement, ran over one enemy submarine; depth-charge attack effective, certain
events.note: Telegram of 7 October 0230, received 0602, its sender column 風早 (Kazahaya); the number is read as written. 1830 I is 1930 K: TINOSA's "1933(K) Target disappeared, sinking by the stern" (rg367-74856215/p08). Five hits in all, against TINOSA's report's "at least six effective hits" of her own and three of STEELHEAD's, and the first endorsement's nine (p34). If the five are J01's one and J02's three, one remains for the evening. Six submarines and four engagements are her count; only TINOSA and STEELHEAD are known to have attacked her. The four characters after 1727 are faint: read as 罐室被雷 (boiler room torpedoed), the first character the old form of 缶, with the help of the same words in Prince Takamatsu's diary as quoted on Japanese Wikipedia (header). So the 1727 engagement of J05 was a hit: TINOSA's 3(b) fired at 1825 K (1725 I) at 1,350 yards, about a minute's run; 3(a) at 1818 K (1718 I), nine minutes earlier, with two hits seen. No position

pairs.note: Fired four stern torpedoes at 02-36-30 K (0136 I) at 10-26N 146-29.5E, a single unescorted tanker, two hits and a dud; the order has Kazahaya torpedoed once at 0244 I at 10-30N 146-37E, about 8 nm away. Hit, not probable: no other boat is known to have attacked her before TINOSA's 1101 I, and STEELHEAD's narrative heard the target "running irregularly" after the hits, as the order has her able to proceed. The times are 68 minutes apart (japanese.yml header); the place, the lone tanker and the day carry the pairing

record.original: YB信令第三六號 二水戦司令官ハ速ニ駆逐艦一隻ヲ派遣風早（〇二四四一〇度三〇分北一四六度三七分東ニ於テ雷撃一ヲ受ク自力航行可能）ノ護衛ニ任ゼシムベシ
record.translation: YB signal order No. 36: the commander of the 2nd Destroyer Squadron is to send one destroyer at once to escort Kazahaya (torpedoed once at 0244 at 10°30'N 146°37'E; able to proceed under her own power)
record.note: TINOSA's J01, the order of 6 October 0830. The position is about 8 nm east-north-east of the 10-26N 146-29.5E STEELHEAD's attack sheet types (rg367-74851315/p22). One torpedo hit, where the sheet has two hits and a dud (Hit, Hit, Dud, Miss) and the narrative a third torpedo striking the forecastle without exploding (p04); "able to proceed under her own power" fits the narrative: 0238 K "Target opened fire with bow gun and turned towards us", and the heavier screws "running irregularly" heard after 0246 K (p05). The time is 68 minutes after STEELHEAD's 0136 I (0236 K): see the header

pairs.note: The Navy's summary starts the attacks at 0140 I, four minutes after STEELHEAD fired (0136 I). It repeats the Combined Fleet's signals (J03), so it is the same witness, not a second one

record.original: 特務艦風早（一二〇〇〇屯 一六．五節 TO）ハ単独トラックニ向ケ航行中トラックノNW二五〇′ニテ敵潜ノ襲撃ヲウク（GF） 敵一隻ヲ乗切リ有効ナル攻撃ヲ加ヘシモ前後五本ノ魚雷ヲ蒙リ一八三〇沈没
record.translation: The special service ship Kazahaya (12,000 tons, 16.5 knots, TO), on passage alone to Truk, was attacked by an enemy submarine 250 miles north-west of Truk (GF). She ran over one of the enemy and attacked it effectively, but took five torpedoes in all and sank at 1830
record.note: TINOSA's J08 (handwritten; numerals as written in Arabic figures on the page). `time` is the entry's, 0140, the start of the attacks: four minutes after STEELHEAD fired at 0136 I (0236 K). "On passage alone" fits the sheet's "Single tanker, unescorted". Compiled from the Combined Fleet's signals, so it counts once with J03. The 250 miles north-west of Truk is the day's later attacks (TINOSA's, near 10-20N 148-30E), not STEELHEAD's position, which is about 360 nm from Truk

pairs.note: She sank at 1830 I, after TINOSA's three attacks (ss-283-tinosa/patrol-3:Attack 2, Attack 3A-3F). STEELHEAD's hit began it ("from 0100 yesterday", the first of four engagements) and slowed her, but the loss can't be given to one attack. JANAC credits her jointly to TINOSA and STEELHEAD (janac:6/p56); ComSubPac credited STEELHEAD with a tanker damaged, 10,500 tons (endorsement, rg367-74851315/p37)

record.original: 二四駆機密第〇七〇二三〇番電 一、昨〇一〇〇以後敵潜水艦六隻ヲ見四回ニ亘リテ交戦被雷計五 二、一七二七罐室被雷一八三〇沈没 三、機密図書処分完了 四、一一〇五第三回交戦ノ際敵潜水艦一隻ヲ乗切リ爆雷攻撃効果確実
record.translation: 1. From 0100 yesterday sighted six enemy submarines and engaged them four times; torpedo hits five in all. 2. 1727 boiler room torpedoed, 1830 sank. 3. Disposal of secret documents completed. 4. At 1105, in the third engagement, ran over one enemy submarine; depth-charge attack effective, certain
record.note: TINOSA's J06, telegram of 7 October 0230, sender 風早 (Kazahaya). "From 0100 yesterday" opens her day with STEELHEAD's attack (0136 I). The 1105 engagement she calls the third is TINOSA's Attack 2, so the first and second were before it; only STEELHEAD's is known. Of the five hits, J01 gives STEELHEAD one and TINOSA's morning attack three (TINOSA's J02). She sank at 1830 I, sixteen hours after STEELHEAD's attack and about 120 nm east of it

pairs.note: TINOSA fired six at 1201 K (table 0204 GCT) and heard three explosions and a dud (narrative, rg367-74856215/p06); Kazahaya signalled three hits at 1210 I (J02) and put the attack at 1105 I (J04, J06), TINOSA's 1201-1204 K less the hour between the zones. Her 1200 position, 10-30N 148-20E, is about 11 nm from the table's 10-35N 148-30E. She claimed the submarine sunk by depth charges (J04); TINOSA took four close charges at 1209 K

record.original: 風早機密第〇六一二一〇番電 我敵潜ノ雷撃ヲ受ク三発命中航行覚束ナシ 北緯一〇度三〇分東経一四八度二〇分
record.translation: Kazahaya secret telegram 061210: we have been torpedoed by an enemy submarine, three hits, our ability to steam is in doubt. 10°30'N 148°20'E
record.note: 1210 is the telegram's time; her later telegrams put this attack at 1105 (J04, J06), which is TINOSA's Attack 2 (narrative 1201 K, 1101 I; table 0204 GCT, 1104 I). The Combined Fleet's order of 1352 (p25) gives 10°30'N 148°20'E as her 1200 position. TINOSA's table types 10-35N 148-30E. Three hits, as TINOSA heard three explosions and a dud (narrative, rg367-74856215/p06)

intelligence.note: A route plotted from a message, its points numbered by day, ending at Truk after 1900 on the 6th; the red star marks the day-6 point. Its date-time group, 271500, fits the intercept combinedfleet describes for Kazahaya (a message decrypted on 27 September giving her departure from Kure on the 30th at 14.5 knots, due at Truk at 0700 on the 7th): candidate, because the ship's name was not in the view read. The star is the route's planned point, not a reported one: Kazahaya was torpedoed on the 6th at 0244 I at 10-30N 146-37E (STEELHEAD; japanese.yml J01), at 1105 I near 10-30N 148-20E (TINOSA's Attack 2; J02) and sank at 1830 I near 9-50N 148-24E (J05, J06), all within about 100 nm of it
intelligence.text: 6 (a red star on the point marked 6 of the route labelled 271500; the next point 1900 / 6)

pairs.note: DesDiv 24 gives 1727 I as the time of her engagement with the submarine (J05). 3A fired four at 1818 K (1718 I), two seen to hit (remarks, rg367-74856215/p17); 3B fired two at 1825 K (1725 I), none seen. The record doesn't say which, so both are possible

record.original: 二四駆機密第〇六二〇一〇番電 二一四五風早遭難推定位置（一七二七敵潜水艦ト交戦地點九度五〇分N一四八度二四分E）ニ到着セシモ見当ラズ今ヨリ捜索ス 明朝ヨリ飛行機ノ協力ヲ得度
record.translation: DesDiv 24 secret telegram 062010: at 2145 arrived at Kazahaya's estimated position of distress (1727, the point of engagement with the enemy submarine, 9°50'N 148°24'E) but she is not in sight; now searching. Request aircraft cooperation from tomorrow morning
record.note: `time` is the engagement's, 1727. The telegram is numbered 062010 but its text reads 2145 for the arrival, so one of the two is misread or mistyped; neither is used. TINOSA fired 3(a) at 1818 K (1718 I) and 3(b) at 1825 K (1725 I) (rg367-74856215/p07). The position is about 13 nm south-west of the 10-01N 148-31E that TINOSA's table types for every evening attack

pairs.note: Fired at 1825 K (1725 I) at 1,350 yards, about a minute's run before the 1727 I of J05, which Kazahaya's own summary calls the boiler room torpedoed (J06). The table claims 0 hits; the commanding officer believed "these mark XVIII may have hit because shortly thereafter the ship stopped dead in the water" (remarks, rg367-74856215/p17). The time fits 3B better than 3A, but a minute or two in a telegram's time can't settle it, so both stay possible

record.original: 二四駆機密第〇六二〇一〇番電 二一四五風早遭難推定位置（一七二七敵潜水艦ト交戦地點九度五〇分N一四八度二四分E）ニ到着セシモ見当ラズ今ヨリ捜索ス 明朝ヨリ飛行機ノ協力ヲ得度
record.translation: DesDiv 24 secret telegram 062010: at 2145 arrived at Kazahaya's estimated position of distress (1727, the point of engagement with the enemy submarine, 9°50'N 148°24'E) but she is not in sight; now searching. Request aircraft cooperation from tomorrow morning
record.note: `time` is the engagement's, 1727. The telegram is numbered 062010 but its text reads 2145 for the arrival, so one of the two is misread or mistyped; neither is used. TINOSA fired 3(a) at 1818 K (1718 I) and 3(b) at 1825 K (1725 I) (rg367-74856215/p07). The position is about 13 nm south-west of the 10-01N 148-31E that TINOSA's table types for every evening attack

pairs.note: Kazahaya sank at 1830 I (J06), TINOSA's 1933 K "Target disappeared, sinking by the stern" (p08). JANAC credits her jointly to TINOSA and STEELHEAD (janac:6/p56: 6 October 1943, Kazahaya, tanker, 8,000 tons, 10-01N 148-31E, "Tinosa Steelhead", sunk), and in the merchant list to "Submarine", not marked probable, at 8,000e tons (janac:4/p45). Probable, not hit: STEELHEAD hit her first (J01), so the loss can't be given to one attack. Her own count is five hits in four engagements (J06): if that is one of STEELHEAD's and three of TINOSA's morning attack, one hit was made in the evening, against the four TINOSA's table claims for 3A, 3D and 3F. The second endorsement credits TINOSA with "1 AO (Type undetermined) 10,000 tons" sunk (p35); her crew called her "the OBSTINATE MARU" (p30)

pairs.note: The table puts the sinking against this shot ("10000 plus same as 2"), but nothing was heard or seen of it (narrative, rg367-74856215/p08); the remarks give the sinking to "one of these last two torpedoes" (3E or 3F, p18). At 1913 K, 1813 I, seventeen minutes before the 1830 I of J06. Probable for the same reason as 3A

record.original: 二四駆機密第〇七〇二三〇番電 一、昨〇一〇〇以後敵潜水艦六隻ヲ見四回ニ亘リテ交戦被雷計五 二、一七二七罐室被雷一八三〇沈没 三、機密図書処分完了 四、一一〇五第三回交戦ノ際敵潜水艦一隻ヲ乗切リ爆雷攻撃効果確実

words.description: Single tanker, unescorted. Original contact by radar at 15,000 yards. Visual contact made at 9,000 yards.
words.determined_by: Damaged Determined by torpedo hits and explosions observed by officers and men on the bridge. Tanker in crippled condition later reported sunk by U.S.S. TINOSA.
words.target_line: Target Draft - 22 feet; Course - 035°, Speed 15 knots, Range-1100 yds
words.own_ship: Speed 10 knots; Course 148°; Depth - surface; Angle 0° (at firing).
words.fire_control: While running at flank speed attempting to get ahead of the target we were evidently sighted at a range of 7000 yards as the tanker changed course 90° and headed directly for us after being on the previous leg only two minutes. It is believed we were mistaken for an escort for the target did not change course again until we had fired. At 2,000 yards he evidently dropped a depth charge to make certain we were not a submarine and as we did not dive he continued on his course. At 1800 yards we were challenged by blinker gun with "AA" and when we did not reply, at 1400 yards he flashed his red and green battle lights three times. We were keeping our stern to the target and were waiting for a 110° starboard track. When the desired track was obtained, fired four torpedoes from stern tubes while still on the surface at a range of 1100 yards. As stated in narrative two hits and one low order detonation believed to be a dud were observed. Because the gunfire at this range was fairly accurate and in order to avoid ramming (target turned towards us after sustaining hits) dove to 80 feet. Had intended to come immediately to periscope depth and resume attack when the sound report of fast light screws and one depth charge, gave the impression that an escort was present and we went deep. The only explanation for the sound report in the light of subsequent actions is that the operator either heard one of our own torpedoes still running or some auxiliary pumps or machinery operating on the target. Because of this erroneous report and the SJ radar failure valuable time was lost before surfacing and the target was never relocated again.
words.torpedo_detail: Mark 14-3A torpedoes (serials 39502, 25474, 23893, 23557), Mark 6-1 exploders (4922, 11310, 17784, 6325), actuation set Contact only, actuation actual blank, Mark 16 warheads (3605, 3633, 843, 10048), TPX. Depth set 12, power High, erratic No on all four.
words.remarks: Torpedo performance was normal. There was some evidence of one dud or low order explosion.
words.note: The sheet types 146-29.5E; the narrative's day position (p04) and ship contact 3 (p19) type 142-29.5E, a typo (positions.csv). The narrative times the firing at 0236 and the hits at 0237; the sheet 02-36-30. The narrative puts the first contact at 120 T. 15,000 yards and the base course 035, speed 15, as the sheet; ship contact 3 types BC-085. The table types "Similar to KYOKUTO MARU". The tanker's depth charge at 2,000 yards (sheet) and the one heard at 0241 after diving (narrative p05) are two events. The sheet claims one damaged; the first endorsement (p34) "two hits and one dud ... severely damaged and later reported sunk by the TINOSA"; ComSubPac's endorsement (p37) credits STEELHEAD with "1 - Tanker (class unknown) - 10,500 tons" damaged.

words.narrative: 1155(K) Sound reported target slowing down. We had been tracking her at 16 knots. 1201(K) Fired six torpedoes from bow tubes. 1202(K) Momentarily ducked. Heard three loud explosions plus a metallic click as of a dud between first and second explosions. Explosions clearly heard through hull. 1204(K) Target began taking starboard list and was down by bow. ... Depth charges and gun fire from target.
words.remarks: In spite of having been hit with three torpedoes by the STEELHEAD the tanker was making 16 knots most of the morning. About five minutes before firing she was heard to slow down and tracked at 11.5 knots. ... The first four torpedoes fired, the inner ones of the spread, were heard to hit, the second being a dud. ... The target was not stopped and attempts to bring the stern tubes to bear were not successful in time to fire them.
words.basis: hit (Hit on the first four rows, Miss on the last two) from the remarks, rg367-74856215/p16, with the table's count of 4; the rest from the summary table, p19.
words.note: The second row's hit was a dud (remarks, p16; the narrative's "metallic click", p06): the table counts it among its 4 hits and so does the CSV. The narrative fires at 1201 K (0201 GCT), three minutes before the table's 0204. The target is the tanker of ship contact 3 (p13), first sighted at 0524 K that morning. She dropped four depth charges, "all close", at 1209 K and started a fire in the motor room (narrative, p06; VIII, p21).

words.narrative: 1644(K) Submerged for approach. ... She started off at about nine knots zigzagging and decreased to about six knots, not zigzagging, when we fired. 1818(K) Fired four torpedoes, stern tubes. Two hits.
words.remarks: ... it was planned to fire a port track with the stern tubes, silhouetting the target against the western horizon. Just as the time arrived to change course, the target changed base course to her left forcing us to use a starboard track and a greater range than we wished. Four torpedoes were fired and the left-hand two were seen and heard to hit, the first just abaft amidships, the second at the stern. With the spread used at least one other torpedo should have hit forward. ... The explosions of the torpedoes were not nearly so loud in the conning tower as previous ones had been. In fact, I did not hear them at all, but saw flames from the after hit and a very large splash from the one about amidships.
words.basis: Everything from the summary table, rg367-74856215/p19. hit is blank: the remarks (p17) say "the left-hand two" hit, which is their place in the spread, not in the order of firing.
words.note: The table types the track as 110P; the remarks say the change of the target's course forced "a starboard track". The CSV keeps 110P. The narrative's 1818 K is the table's 0818 GCT. The table's footnotes: "#Should have been three hits. *See VII Particulars of Attacks - Remarks."

words.narrative: 1821(K) Target began dropping and throwing depth charges and firing with both guns. Eight depth charges in all were used. Target began turn to her right as if to ram as she had done during morning attack. ... Target swung past ramming course and was making about five knots. 1825(K) Fired two bow tubes. No indication of hits or explosions but shortly thereafter target stopped. List had increased slightly but there was no evidence of sinking. Gun fire continued.
words.remarks: ... We fired two bow tubes as indicated in the table. The set up looked good but no explosions resulted. The torpedoes were heard to run on the correct course. The target's swing was undoubtedly due to the previous hit aft disabling the starboard screw. I believe these mark XVIII may have hit because shortly thereafter the ship stopped dead in the water, whereas she ran for at least six minutes after attack #3a.
words.basis: hit (Miss on both rows) from the table's 0 hits, rg367-74856215/p19; the rest from the same table.
words.note: The table's 0 hits stands in the CSV; the commanding officer believed "these mark XVIII may have hit" (remarks, p17). The narrative fires at 1825 K, a minute after the table's 0824 GCT.

words.narrative: 1834(K) After maneuvering to obtain position desired fired one stern tube using 180 gyro angle, spindle disengaged and 180 periscope angle. Mark XIV torpedo ran straight at target but no splash was seen. Target opened fire as soon as wake of torpedo was visible and explosions of shells were numerous. Growing darker.
words.remarks: Ship was dead in water but giving no evidence of sinking. Rapidly growing darker. Obtained position and fired one mark XIV which was seen and heard to run straight to target. Used 180 gyro angle and periscope angle, spindle disengaged. No evidence of explosion or hit.
words.basis: hit (Miss) from the table's 0 hits for its one torpedo, rg367-74856215/p20; the rest from the same table.
words.note: The narrative fires at 1834 K, a minute after the table's 0833 GCT.

words.narrative: 1859(K) Boats had been lowered by target and were heard in water but occasional gun fire continued. After maneuvering for position fired stern tube, using 180 gyro, spindle disengaged. Torpedo ran straight to target and sound reported an explosion at proper time interval. None seen or heard by officer at periscope.
words.remarks: Same as #3c except that sound and people in control room reported an explosion. I saw torpedo wake but no evidence of explosion.
words.basis: hit (Hit) from the table's 1 hit for its one torpedo, rg367-74856215/p20; the rest from the same table.
words.note: The table's hit rests on sound and the control room; the officer at the periscope saw none (narrative, p07). The narrative's 1859 K is the table's 0859 GCT.

words.narrative: 1910(K) With gun fire still occasionally occurring and no evidence of sinking maneuvered and fired bow tube, zero gyro, spindle disengaged. Sound tracked torpedo running straight for target but heard no explosion. None seen.
words.remarks: Maneuvered for bow shot. Fired zero gyro and periscope angle, spindles disengaged. No evidence of hit, visual or aural.
words.basis: hit (Miss) from the table's 0 hits for its one torpedo, rg367-74856215/p20; the rest from the same table.
words.note: The narrative fires at 1910 K, a minute after the table's 0909 GCT.

words.narrative: 1913(K) Fired second bow tube, same conditions. Heard to run straight for target but no explosion and none seen. These two torpedoes were not even heard to hit. Target still seemed to have lots of buoyancy. 1923(K) ... Target now showed first evidence of sinking, the stern being down and settling fast. 1933(K) Target disappeared, sinking by the stern. STEELHEAD had made three hits on this target. We had at least six effective hits, ie. torpedoes which detonated.
words.remarks: Same as 3e. One of these last two torpedoes must have been effective because shortly thereafter the ship began sinking rapidly. This might possibly have been caused by the collapse of bulkheads but there was no evidence of sinking prior to attacks 3e and 3f.
words.basis: hit (Hit) from the table's 1 hit for its one torpedo, rg367-74856215/p20; the rest from the same table.
words.note: The table types a hit and the sinking against this torpedo, but the narrative heard and saw no explosion from it ("These two torpedoes were not even heard to hit", p08), and the remarks give the sinking to "one of these last two" (p18): the hit is the table's inference from the sinking, not an observed hit. The CSV keeps the table's Hit. In XVIII Remarks (p30) "the sound operator heard one explode" of the last four shots, which is 3(d). The first endorsement (p34): "It is almost certain that the ship absorbed nine torpedo hits before sinking"; the second (p35) recommends "1 AO (Type undetermined) 10,000 tons" sunk.
